title: Constant-tower and semilinear-counit normalizations of integral compactification composition agree
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and put $h=gf$. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\widehat R_T=\lim_n(A_n)_T$. Use the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_T$, reduction/total-limit adjunction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$, and its actual unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $K$ be derived-complete constructible with finite Tor amplitude. Require every system and intermediate object below to have compatible etale-origin witnesses and normalized reductions, with cohomological and Tor amplitudes in common finite intervals, as specified in [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization].

Choose a compatible tower of compactifications $c_f,c_g,c_h$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]: each $c_v=(j_v,p_v)$ has $j_v$ quasi-compact open, $p_v$ proper, and $v=p_vj_v$, and the compatible intermediate proper/open square supplies the compactification of $h$. Write $B_v=S_{p_v}J_{j_v}$ on semilinear systems, with system direct image $S$ and termwise open extension $J$. Let $\beta:B_gB_f\to B_h$ be the compactification composition map formed from the canonical proper/open map $\Gamma_Q$ and the unital direct-image/open compositors of [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting]. Let $F_v=Rv_!$ be exactly the integral reduction-tower functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Denote by
$$d_{v,M}:\mathcal L B_v\mathcal R M\xrightarrow{\sim}F_vM$$
the direct identification with that functor's defining strict quotient tower and total-limit model, with its specified quotient transitions. These are direct identifications for a single compactification, rather than an unspecified choice of the expression-realization family $c_V$. For the identity compactification $(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$, after the canonical system unitors identify $B_{\mathrm{id}}$ with $1$, one has $F_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathcal L\mathcal R$ and $d_{\mathrm{id},M}=1_{\mathcal L\mathcal R M}$.

For constant $R$-module coordinates, let $H_T$ be restriction along $\underline R_T\to\widehat R_T$ on complete complexes, the equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Use the strict constant towers and their total-limit functor $\mathcal L^{\mathcal T}$ and reduction $\mathcal R^{\mathcal T}$. Let $W_v$ be the word consisting of proper direct image after completed open extension for $c_v$, and $\widetilde W_v$ its strict constant-tower word. Let
$$a_{v,K}:H(F_vK)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L^{\mathcal T}\widetilde W_v\mathcal R^{\mathcal T}(HK),\qquad
 a_{g,f,K}:H(F_gF_fK)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L^{\mathcal T}\widetilde W_g\widetilde W_f\mathcal R^{\mathcal T}(HK)$$
be precisely the normalized word comparisons $a_W=\mathcal L^{\mathcal T}(q_W)\eta$, with the recursive $q_W$ and generator normalizations of [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit], using the canonical compact-support and constant/completed coefficient identifications. The single-compactification identifications here use the canonical direct-image/derived-limit comparison and the open comparison fixed by reduction of the completion unit, as specified by the same word-comparison theorem; they are not arbitrary isomorphisms between these functors. Let $\beta^{\mathcal T}$ be the constant-tower proper/open composition map for the same compactification tower, formed from the normalized strict-tower proper/open comparison $\gamma_Q$ and the canonical direct-image and open-extension compositors of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], and let $\alpha^{\mathrm{cbc}}_{g,f}:F_gF_f\to F_h$ be the specified completed composition comparison in [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4); in these coordinates its components are
$$H(\alpha^{\mathrm{cbc}}_{g,f,K})=a_{h,K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L^{\mathcal T}(\beta^{\mathcal T})\circ a_{g,f,K}.$$
Then the following is an equality of actual integral morphisms $F_gF_fK\to F_hK$:
$$\alpha^{\mathrm{cbc}}_{g,f,K}
=d_{h,K}\circ\mathcal L_Z(\beta_{\mathcal R_XK})\circ\mathcal L_Z\bigl(B_g(e_{B_f\mathcal R_XK})\bigr)\circ\mathcal L_ZB_g\mathcal R_Y(d_{f,K}^{-1})\circ d_{g,F_fK}^{-1}.$$
The equality is natural in $K$ for the supplied compatible compactification tower, including towers with an identity or empty open. It compares the specified constant-tower word normalization and the specified semilinear counit normalization before any finite evaluation; no arbitrary choice of intertwining realizations is used.

source.place: Step 5, compatibility with compact-support composition; additional agent-formulated comparison obligation between the explicit constant-tower word construction and the semilinear reduction/total-limit construction. This equality is not stated in the blueprint.

proof.text: Write $U_T$ for termwise restriction of a semilinear system to a constant $R$-module tower. Use the canonical identifications $U\mathcal R=\mathcal R^{\mathcal T}H$ and $H\mathcal L=\mathcal L^{\mathcal T}U$; restriction carries the actual quotient completion unit $u$ to $\eta$. For each proper or open letter use the canonical operation identification and the equality $U(r_A)=q_A$ of the single-generator comparison. All suppressed identifications below are these natural identifications. This fixes the coordinate change on derived strict towers, including morphisms; it does not require scalar restriction to be faithful.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram; agent argument with the specified generator comparison and quotient-unit normalization.
Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, for the strict total-limit model; formal unit naturality and right triangle identity.

proof.text:
Fix one of $c_v=(j,p)$, put $N_j=J_j\mathcal RM$, and let $D=j_!M$. The specified open comparison is $d_j:\mathcal LN_j\to D$. The canonical identification of $Rp_*D$ with the defining compact-support tower identifies $d_{v,M}^{-1}$ with $b_{p,N_j}Rp_*(d_j^{-1})$. This is precisely the direct-image/limit comparison followed by the prescribed open comparison, as required in the statement; no expression-realization $c_V$ is chosen. Put $r_v=(S_pr_j)r_{p,D}$. Naturality of $b_p$ and the preceding step yield
$$\mathcal L(r_v)u_{Rp_*D}=\mathcal LS_p(r_j)b_{p,\mathcal RD}Rp_*(u_D)
=b_{p,N_j}Rp_*(\mathcal L(r_j)u_D)
=b_{p,N_j}Rp_*(d_j^{-1})=d_{v,M}^{-1}.$$
The adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal R F_vM,B_v\mathcal RM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_vM,\mathcal LB_v\mathcal RM)$ sends $r$ to $\mathcal L(r)u$. Its inverse therefore gives
$$r_{v,M}=e_{B_v\mathcal RM}\circ\mathcal R(d_{v,M}^{-1}).$$

source.place: Agent calculation on the specified strict quotient towers; Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, and the fixed open reduction comparison.

proof.text:
Apply $U$ to the definition $r_v=(S_pr_j)r_{p,D}$. The single-generator equalities of Step 1 and the recursive word normalization give
$$U(r_v)=(\widetilde S_p q_j)q_{p,J_j^cHM}=q_{W_v,HM}.$$
Here $HD=J_j^cHM$ is the fixed completed-open identification. This is equality in the derived strict-tower category: both sides are the composite of the same two one-letter maps. The two-letter calculation in Step 3 shows why the resulting $r_v$ uses the direct $d_v$ in the question, rather than an unspecified expression realization.

source.place: Agent substitution in the recursive word normalization; Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, underlies the generator comparison.

proof.text:
For each $v$ and allowed input $M$, use Step 4, preservation of the completion unit, and the defining formula for $a$ to obtain
$$a_{v,M}=\mathcal L^{\mathcal T}(U r_{v,M})H(u_{F_vM})
=H\bigl(\mathcal L(r_{v,M})u_{F_vM}\bigr)=H(d_{v,M}^{-1}).$$
Equivalently, substituting Step 3 gives the explicit cancellation
$$\mathcal L(e_{B_v\mathcal RM})\mathcal L\mathcal R(d_{v,M}^{-1})u_{F_vM}
=\mathcal L(e_{B_v\mathcal RM})u_{\mathcal LB_v\mathcal RM}d_{v,M}^{-1}=d_{v,M}^{-1}.$$
Thus the single-word comparisons match the required direct identifications as maps before finite evaluation.

source.place: Formal unit naturality and right triangle identity on the strict total-limit model of Tag 0941.

proof.text:
For the concatenated word $W_gW_f$, use the recursive $q$ formula followed by Step 5 at the input $F_fK$:
$$a_{g,f,K}=\mathcal L^{\mathcal T}(\widetilde W_gq_{W_f,HK})a_{g,F_fK}
=H\bigl(\mathcal L_Z(B_gr_{f,K})d_{g,F_fK}^{-1}\bigr).$$
Insert the actual transpose from Step 3:
$$a_{g,f,K}=H\bigl(\mathcal L_Z(B_g(e_{B_f\mathcal R_XK}))\,
\mathcal L_ZB_g\mathcal R_Y(d_{f,K}^{-1})\,d_{g,F_fK}^{-1}\bigr).$$
All these expressions are defined: the hypotheses supply the normalized systems, etale-origin witnesses and common finite amplitude bounds for $K$, $F_fK$ and the intermediate proper/open operations. Only functoriality distributes $B_g$ and $\mathcal L_Z$ over the two factors.

source.place: Agent substitution in the recursive word comparison; no exchange-pasting assertion or finite-evaluation criterion is used.

proof.text:
The semilinear system realization identifies the restriction of $\Gamma_Q$ with the normalized strict constant-tower $\gamma_Q$. Both $\beta$ and $\beta^{\mathcal T}$ are assembled from this map and the canonical direct-image and open compositors. The one-letter scalar comparisons preserve the adjunction units and counits. Since the compositors are adjunction conjugates, mate pasting identifies their scalar-restriction comparisons with the canonical constant-tower compositors. Consequently
$$U(\beta_{\mathcal R_XK})=\beta^{\mathcal T}_{\mathcal R_X^{\mathcal T}HK},\qquad
H\mathcal L_Z(\beta_{\mathcal R_XK})=\mathcal L_Z^{\mathcal T}(\beta^{\mathcal T}).$$
This uses the stated comparison of actual strict-system transformations, rather than comparison of their evaluations. The supplied compatible compactification tower gives exactly the same intermediate proper/open square on both sides.

source.place: Tags 0F7B/0F7C/0F7D, more-etale.tex, proper/open composition; their specified semilinear/constant-tower normalization is supplied by the cited statements.

proof.text:
Substitute Steps 5--7 into the stipulated defining equation
$$H(\alpha^{\mathrm{cbc}}_{g,f,K})=a_{h,K}^{-1}\mathcal L^{\mathcal T}(\beta^{\mathcal T})a_{g,f,K}.$$
It becomes the image under $H$ of
$$d_{h,K}\mathcal L_Z(\beta_{\mathcal R_XK})\mathcal L_Z(B_g(e_{B_f\mathcal R_XK}))\mathcal L_ZB_g\mathcal R_Y(d_{f,K}^{-1})d_{g,F_fK}^{-1}.$$
The source and target are derived-complete integral objects, where $H$ is an equivalence and hence faithful. Equality of these two images therefore gives the asserted equality of integral morphisms. Naturality follows because each factor used above is a natural transformation, so the calculation applies to every morphism between the allowed inputs.

source.place: Agent substitution and faithfulness of the complete-category equivalence; the displayed formula for alpha is part of the item data.

proof.text: For an identity compactification $B_{\mathrm{id}}=1$ and $d_{\mathrm{id},M}=1$, Step 3 reads $r_{\mathrm{id},M}=e_{\mathcal RM}$. Since $u_M$ is invertible, the left triangle gives $e_{\mathcal RM}=\mathcal R(u_M^{-1})$; thus the empty constant word, transported from $M$ to $F_{\mathrm{id}}M=\mathcal L\mathcal RM$ by $u_M^{-1}$, has exactly this comparison. Step 5 then reads $a_{\mathrm{id},M}=1$, since $\mathcal L(e_{\mathcal RM})u_{\mathcal L\mathcal RM}=1$. Inserting an identity therefore requires no extra unitor or arbitrary automorphism. For an empty open, extension by zero is the zero functor: the input from the empty site and all its proper/open images are zero, so both sides are the unique map between zero objects. These checks also cover a zero input.

source.place: Formal identity and zero-object cases, with the actual reduction/limit triangle identities.
